paragraphs: En haishsha ola mittumatah ad shettitbol et kol gupah im kol saaroteha bebat-achat beme mayan o miqveh sheyyesh bahem arbaim sea. vetzarik sheyyaaleh betishboret arbaim vearbaa elep umea ushemoneh asara etzbaot, veod chatzi etzba pachot rebia; vetzarik laasot hacheshbon beetzbaot davqa velo leshaer bemishqal, ki hammedida hi haiqqar; veayyen "shiyyure-beraka". vetzarik sheyyihyu hammayim shebbecharitz gadol yoter mishshiur hannizkar, bikde sheachar shettitbol veyipchatu hammayim mikkenisatah bo, yishshaaru hammayim shiur arbaim sea hannizkar; mihu, "p sheyyesh sham harbeh yoter mearbaim sea, im en gebohim lemala mittabburah zeret shehu shenem asar gudalim - asur litbol bo lekattechilla.

clarification.explanation: A woman does not rise from her impurity until she immerses her entire body, with all her hair, at once, in spring water or a mikveh containing forty se'ah. This measure is calculated by the volume of finger-widths, and must be measured by finger-widths specifically, not estimated by weight. The mikveh must contain more than forty se'ah, so that even after she enters and the water level drops, forty se'ah still remain; and even if the water reaches only up to her navel (a handbreadth above), one should not immerse in it as the primary practice, since the water must rise above the navel.
takeaways: One immerses the entire body and hair at once in a mikveh of forty se'ah.
The water must reach above the navel, and is measured by volume, not weight.

paragraphs: Miqveh zeh shehu kasher litbilat nidda, haynu shehammayim baim min me-geshamim, venopelim mealehem letok hammiqveh; abal mayim sheubim "y adam shennetanam letok hammiqveh, pesulim; mihu, yesh meqomot shehammayim baim venimshakim min hannahar letok hatztzinnorot "y mekona, shemmadliqim esh tachat haddud, umaaleh hebel betok hammukeni veyitgalgel, veal yede kak yaaleh hammayim letok hatztzinnorot shehem petuchim mishshene ebrehem, vehammayim nopelim mealehem tok hatztzinnorot. vekatabti bazeh teshuba beorek bsh"q "rab-pealim", lehattir hammiqveh hannaaseh bekak, "g dezeh naaseh mikkoach haesh asher haadam madliq beyadayim - en bazeh pissul, mishshum daaliyyat hammayim hi naaset "y shelosha kochot bezeh achar zeh; vaapillu dehaggaon "tebuot shor" machmir bekoach kocho - modeh bishlosha kochot. upoh irenu, tehillot lael, sheyyesh lanu borot mayim chayyim bekamma vekamma chatzerot shebbair shebbahem tobelot hannashim, vezeh adip mimmiqveh bekamma peratim; veayyen "sheelat-yabetz", cheleq ', deuvveta napsho meod lebaer-mayim asher mukshar lazzabin, "g deqayma lan keman deamar demiqveh kasher litbilat nidda, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: A valid mikveh is one whose water comes from rainwater falling into it on its own, but water drawn by a person is invalid. In places where water is drawn from a river through pipes by a steam engine and falls in on its own, the rabbi ruled in "Rav Pe'alim" to permit it, since the water's rise is caused by mechanical forces and there is no invalidating "drawing" involved. In Baghdad there were pits of spring water (living water) in many courtyards where women immersed, and this is preferable to a mikveh in several respects.
takeaways: A valid mikveh contains rainwater falling in on its own, not water drawn by a person.
Living (spring) water is preferable to a standard mikveh.

paragraphs: Lo yihyeh aleha dabar chotzetz apillu kol-shehu. veyesh debarim chotzetzin lekattechilla davqa, ubediabad tebilatah keshera; veyesh chotzetzin gam bediabad. al ken im tabela venimtza aleha ezeh dabar, tishal lemoreh, kede ladaat im zeh chotzetz bediabad o lo.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for anything at all to interpose (chatzitzah) on a woman's body during immersion, even the slightest amount. Some things interpose only as the primary rule, while after the fact the immersion is valid; others interpose even after the fact. Therefore, if she immersed and something was found on her, she should ask a halachic authority to determine whether it interposes after the fact, requiring her to immerse again.
takeaways: Any interposition invalidates the immersion; some interpose only as the primary rule, others even after the fact.
If something is found after immersion, one should consult a halachic authority.

paragraphs: Betzoa shettachat hatztzipporen, yesh chilluq ben im hu keneged habbasar leben eno keneged habbasar; ulepi sheen yekolin lekavven mah niqra keneged habbasar, nahagu hannashim littol hatztzipparenayim, ben shel yadayim, ben shel ragliyyim. veim shakecha apillu tzipporen achat vetabela, tzerika tebila acheret. bammeh debarim amurim? im hirgisha betzipporen qodem sheshshimmesha im balah, abal hirgisha achar sheshshimmesha im balah: im yesh tzoa betzipporen shello keneged habbasar, titbol tebila acheret; veim hatztzoa hi keneged habbasar bilbad, lo titbol tebila acheret. ken anachnu morin poh irenu y" meabotenu; mihu im shakecha tzipporen shel ragliyyim davqa, katabti bsh"q "mqbtzl" deyesh lehattir bazeh mishshum sepiq sapeqa; veayyen "pitche-teshuba", seip qatan ch', dibtzipparene ragliyyim yesh lehaqel, ayyen sham. vekol zeh betzoa, abal im yesh batzeq tachat hatztzipporen, apillu keneged habbasar davqa, hare zeh chotzetz utzerika tebila acheret bekol gavna.

clarification.explanation: Dirt under the fingernail interposes in certain cases, and since it is difficult to know what is considered interposing, women were accustomed to trim all their fingernails and toenails. If she forgot even one nail and immersed, she must immerse again; but if she remembers only after having relations with her husband, there is a distinction based on the location of the dirt. Toenails may be treated more leniently. This applies to ordinary dirt, but dough under the nail interposes in any case and requires a separate immersion.
takeaways: It was customary to trim all fingernails and toenails before immersion.
Dough under the nail always interposes.

paragraphs: Im yesh lah nepach al meqom hatztzipporen, veenah yekola lachtok vegam enah yekola lechattet, im hi nepucha kol kak sheen hattit shettachat hatztzipporen nireh, eno chotzetz. veim beshabbat vyv"t shakecha littol tzippareneha mibbeod yom, venizkera achar sheqqadash hayyom, minhagenu lehattir laqutz otah "y goy. veyilmedu et haggoya shehi tiqqach et yede haishsha kede laqutz, vetizzaher gam-ken shello taaseh im haggoya siyyua.

clarification.explanation: If she has swelling at the site of the nail and cannot trim or clean it, and the swelling is so pronounced that the dirt under the nail is not visible — it does not interpose. And on the Sabbath and Festivals, if she forgot to trim her nails beforehand and only remembered after the day began, it was customary to permit trimming them through a gentile woman — she is taught to take the woman's hand and cut, being careful that the woman herself not assist in the act.
takeaways: Swelling that covers dirt under the nail does not interpose.
If forgotten on the Sabbath, a gentile woman trims the nails, without the woman's own assistance.

paragraphs: Chatzitza - lav davqa al gupah, ella apillu bebet-hassetarim sheen hammayim baim shamma, mikkol maqom tzerikin lihyot reuyin lebiat mayim. lepikak tzerika lenaqqot shinneha; veim tabela venimtza aach"k dabar ben shinneha, lo aleta lah tebila. velaken nohagin shello leekol basar bayyom leketem lebet-hattebila, mippene shehabbasar niknas ben hashshinnayim yoter mishshear okel, vechosheshin shemma lo yinqom yapeh. ubeshabbat vyv"t demukrachim leekol basar, yizzaharu lenaqqot yapeh yapeh. vetizzaher kol yom hattebila shello laasoq babbatzeq vekayyotze bidbarim hannidbaqim sheenam oberim min haggup benaqel. veereb shabbat veereb yom tob shemmukrachat laasoq bazeh, tizzaher lirchotz yapeh achar kol eseq, vetasim datah al zeh. vetizzaher shello leekol ben chapipa litbila shum maakol kelal.

clarification.explanation: Interposition invalidates not only on the exposed body but also in "hidden places," where even though the water does not need to actually reach there, it must be fit to reach there. Therefore she must clean her teeth, and if something is found between her teeth, her immersion is invalid. For this reason it was customary not to eat meat on the day of immersion, since it lodges between the teeth more, and on the Sabbath and Festivals, when compelled to eat it, one should clean thoroughly afterward. She should also be careful on the immersion day not to handle dough or sticky substances, and if compelled to, she should wash her hands after any such handling, and not eat at all between the hair-washing and the immersion.
takeaways: Hidden places must also be cleaned; meat is avoided on the immersion day.
One does not eat between the hair-washing and the immersion.

paragraphs: Im shakecha lehaabir sear shel meqom erva - im kebar rachatza oto maqom heteb qodem tebila, velo nishar shum zea veshum dibbuq bassearot, eno chotzetz bediabad; veayyen "shiyyure beraka", seip qatan b'.

clarification.explanation: If she forgot to remove the pubic hair, but had already washed that area well before immersion and no sweat or sticky substance remained on the hairs — it does not interpose after the fact.
takeaways: Forgetting to remove pubic hair, if the area was washed well beforehand, does not interpose after the fact.

paragraphs: Ishah sheyyesh lah shen totebet shel etzem o shel kesep shemmaamidin oto bimqom hashshen shennapal mimmenna kede shello titganneh - heeleti bsh"q "rab-pealim", deim en darkah lahasiro lipamim kede lenaqqoto, eno chotzetz, vikola lekattechilla litbol beodo aleha; abal im darkah lipamim lahasiro kede lenaqqoto, nakon lahasiro qodem tebila, kemo shekkatab harab "meore-esh", yoreh dea, siman h veav; veraq i ikka tircha gedola bahasarato, shetztzerika lelek etzel haumman lahasiro lah mippene shehu qabua bechut kesep, vetzarik umman lahasiro ulehachaziro, veyesh lah busha bedabar zeh shettitparsem tebilatah - yesh lismok al sebarat hammattirim litbol beshen zeh bekol gavna; veen lachush lisbarat haggaon "shoel umeshib" qamma, cheleq g, siman k"z, sheasar vechalaq al hammattir; vekaasher heerakti bs"d bsh"q hannizkar, vedachiti kol reayot shello; veod hebeti sham debarayv b"shoel umeshib" tinyana, cheleq g', sop siman q"ch, shennireh shechazar bo harab missebarato hannizkeret, shehittir sham beenayim "p shellipamim mesira otah, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: A woman with a false tooth (of bone or silver) fixed in place of a fallen tooth: if she is not accustomed to removing it for cleaning — it does not interpose and she may immerse with it in place as the primary practice; and if she is accustomed to removing it occasionally — it is proper to remove it before immersion. But if removing it involves great effort (fixed with a silver wire requiring a craftsman) and she would be embarrassed by her immersion becoming publicly known — one may rely on the lenient authorities to immerse with it in any case.
takeaways: A permanently fixed false tooth that is not normally removed does not interpose.
One normally removed — better to remove before immersion, but in case of great effort or embarrassment one may rely on the lenient view.

paragraphs: Ishah shehittik lah harope operet betok neqeb hashshen shellah lirpua, "g deharab "chakemat-adam" s"l dehave chatzitza, uperesh tamo b"binat-adam", ot y"b - hinneh yesh lehassig al reayot shello; vehaiqqar kehaggaon "shoel umeshib" tinyana, cheleq g', siman q"ch, diplag al "chakemat-adam" vehittir bazeh, yeuyyan sham. veken beseper "chuqqe-daat" katab deah"meir netibim" lmhrsh"k hechlit lehattir, yeuyyan sham; veken harab "nachal-eshkol", chibbur al seper "haeshkol", behilkot miqvaot, siman s"h, ot v', heerik lehattir bazeh, yeuyyan sham. veal-ken heeleti bs"d bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim" lismok al hammattirin, ubiprat shehu midi derabbanan.

clarification.explanation: A woman whose doctor placed a lead filling in a tooth cavity for medical treatment — although some held this interposes, the primary view is to be lenient that it does not, and this is the view of many authorities. Furthermore, this is a rabbinic-level matter, and in a rabbinic doubt one is lenient. Therefore the rabbi ruled to rely on the lenient authorities.
takeaways: A permanent dental filling does not interpose, especially since this is a rabbinic-level matter.

paragraphs: Ishah sheyyesh lah choli ozen, veharope amar im yikkanesu hammayim beavezanah yazziq lah meod - heeleti bsh"q "rab-pealim", deen lah laasot taqqana leatzmah lehannicha tzemer-gepen beazenah kede shello yikkanesu hammayim, ki bazeh have chatzitza; ella taaseh kaopen sheasa harab "shibat-tziyyon" za"l, siman m"b - shettered chabertah immah lammiqveh, vetaamod rachoq mimmenna, vetatbil chabertah et yadah bammiqveh, veaach"k titchob chabertah et etzbaah beazene haishsha hazzot, vetizzaher shello titchob bechozeq ella beripyon qetzat; abal hi atzmah lo tannicha etzbaah beavezanah, ki i epshar lehagbihha yadeha bishat tebila.

clarification.explanation: A woman with an ear ailment, whom the doctor said water entering her ear would greatly harm her — should not place cotton wool in her ear, since this itself interposes. Rather, a female companion should go down with her into the mikveh, immerse her own hand in the water, and then gently insert her finger loosely into the woman's ear, so the water reaches there this way. But the woman herself should not place a finger in her ear, since she cannot raise her hands during the immersion.
takeaways: Cotton wool should not be placed in the ear (it interposes).
A companion plugs the ear with a wet, loose finger instead.

paragraphs: Tzerika lehizzaher laasot hachapipa bayyom hashshebii samuk lattebila. veqodem hachapipa tachtok tzipparene yadeha veragleha, vetasir sear bet-hashshechi veerva bekol open sheyyihyeh - hen "y chut, hen "y taar, hen "y sam - beopen shettasir kol hassear kullo meiqqaro, veaach"k taasoq bachapipa, vekak hi: tirchatz roshah bemayim chammin, vaapillu beposherin o chamme-chamma saggi, vetissareq sear roshah bemasreq heteb shello yihyu hassearot debuqin umequshsharin; vehasseriqa tihyeh bishat rechitza bechammin, shebbazeh yihyeh hassear menuqqeh heteb; veaach"k tirchatz bechammin sear rise eneha, uteshapshep beyadeha lehaprid hassearot shel rise eneha shello yihyu nidbaqin umequshsharin; ubiprat ishah sheyyesh lah mechosh berise eneha, sheddarkam lihyot debuqim zeh im zeh, shetztzerika lasim libbah al niqqayon shellahem heteb. vetizzaher shello yihyeh liplup beeneha - hen mibbipnim, hen mibbachutz, apillu lach; veaach"k tirchatz kol gupah bechammin, vetishtop bishat chapipa gupah vesheyyeareh, vetasir kol lichluchi tzoa sheal besarah shehem mechamat zea; vegam tirchatz heteb ben etzbeot ragleha min haabaq shennidbaq sham, vetinnaqem yapeh ben kol etzba veetzba, velo tishkach achat mehem; uteayyen heteb vetibdoq bekol gupah bekol maqom sheepshar lah libdoq, shello yihyeh aleha dabar chotzetz. veken lipamim yesh mine kinnim metim debuqim bassear, vetashgicha heteb alehem lahasiram. veken tzerika lehasir hatztzoa mittok hachotem bipnim mah sheepshar, abal mah shehu lemala betok hachotem, la chayetz; veken tzerika lehasir tzoat haozen ulenaqqotah yapeh. veyesh nashim sheddarkan leshapshep rosham betit sheqqorin bearbe "tin keuv" (butz rachatza) kede lenaqqoto heteb, umikkocha hashshipshup betit zeh yikkanes min hattit betok haozen, veyidbaq sham bemaqom shehu nireh lakkol; laken tzarik shettasim leb lirchotz azeneha bemayim chammin achar hashshipshup, shemma nishar sham min hattit hazzeh.

clarification.explanation: The hair-washing (chafifah) must be done on the seventh day, close to the immersion. First she trims her fingernails and toenails and removes the underarm and pubic hair at the root, and then washes: she washes her head in hot (or lukewarm) water and combs it well so no hairs remain tangled; she washes and separates her eyelashes and makes sure there is no discharge; she washes her entire body, including between the toes to remove dust, and checks everywhere for anything that might interpose (including dead lice in the hair); and she cleans her nose and ears of dirt. If she washed her head with mud, she should be careful to wash her ears afterward lest mud residue remain there. And whatever is found deep inside the nose — does not interpose.
takeaways: The hair-washing is done on the seventh day, close to immersion, after trimming nails and removing hair.
One washes and checks the entire body, hair, eyelashes, nose, and ears.

paragraphs: "p shessareqa vechapepa bebetah, tissa masreq immah lebet-hattebila, vetisroq sham qodem tebila. v"p shechapepa karauy veayena gupah karauy bishat chapipa, im kol zeh achar shettipshot chaluqah litbol, beodah omedet al sepat hammiqveh, tzerika leayyen velibdoq gupah bekol maqom sheepshar lirot; vegam temashmesh beyadeha uberoshah vegabbah libdoq im yesh sham dabar chotzetz. veiyyun ubediqa zo hi middeorayta, velaken tzarik lehizzaher bah meod shello tishkachenna.

clarification.explanation: Even though she combed and washed at home, she should bring a comb to the immersion house and comb there again before immersing. And after removing her robe, while standing at the edge of the mikveh, she must examine and inspect her entire body wherever visible, and run her hands over her head and back to check for any interposition. This examination close to the immersion is Torah-mandated, and therefore one must be very careful not to forget it.
takeaways: She combs and examines herself again at the edge of the mikveh before immersing.
This examination is Torah-mandated — it must not be forgotten.

paragraphs: Chal tebilatah belel motzae-shabbat, shei epshar lah lechop bayyom, tichop beereb-shabbat, vetachazor bemotzae-shabbat lechop velisroq meat bechammin; veken im chal tebilatah bemotzae yv"t; veken im chal yv"t beyom chamishi veshishshi, vechala tebilatah bemotzae-shabbat - tichop beyom d' shehu ereb yv"t, vetiqshor saaroteha vetishmerem shello yitbalbelu. vetizzaher beotam hayyamim shebben chapipa litbila shello yidbaq bah meuma min maakol umashqeh sheddarkan lehiddabeq bebasar. veim hi aqeret-habbayit utzerika laasoq beyadeha veliga bidbarim hannidbaqim, tirchatz yadeha achar kol paam sheoseqet. ubelel tebilatah: im hu chol hammoed, taaseh chammin vetirchatz vetisroq qodem tebila; veim hu shabbat achar yv"t, teayyen heteb vetibdoq gupah usearot roshah shello yihyeh dabar chotzetz, vetadicha bet-hassetarim bemayim chammin shehuchammu byv"t, abal lo tirchatz kol gupah; vetinnaqeh shinneha qodem tebila, shello yishshaer basar velo shum perurin, vetitbol.

clarification.explanation: If her immersion falls on the night after the Sabbath and hair-washing during the day is impossible, she should wash on Sabbath eve and return after the Sabbath's conclusion to comb briefly in hot water; the same applies after a Festival's conclusion. When a Festival falls on Thursday and Friday and her immersion is the night after the following Sabbath, she should wash on Wednesday (the Festival eve), tie up her hair, and keep it protected. During the days between the hair-washing and the immersion she should be careful that no food or drink sticks to her. On the immersion night: during Chol HaMoed she should wash and comb in hot water before immersing; and on a Sabbath following a Festival, she should examine and inspect her body and hair, rinse hidden places with water heated on the Festival (but not wash her whole body), and clean her teeth.
takeaways: Immersion after the Sabbath or a Festival — she washes beforehand and combs again afterward.
She is careful between the washing and immersion, and re-examines herself on the immersion night.

paragraphs: Tzarik laamod al gabbah yehudit gedola bat y"b shana veyom echad beshaa shettobelet, kede shettireh shello yishshaer sear echad missearot roshah tzap al-pene hammayim. veim yesh sapeq shemma nishar mashshehu bachutz, apillu bediabad lo aleta lah tebila. velo teechoz bah chabertah bishat tebila; ubishat haddechaq shetztzerika lekak, az chabertah titbol yadah techilla bammiqveh vetochaz bah beripyon.

clarification.explanation: An adult Jewish woman over twelve years and a day must stand behind her during the immersion to make sure not a single hair remains floating above the water's surface. If there is doubt whether something remained outside the water, even after the fact the immersion is not valid. Her companion does not hold onto her during the immersion, but in a pressing situation where support is needed, the companion should first immerse her own hand in the mikveh and then hold her loosely.
takeaways: An adult woman watches to ensure no hair floats above the water.
No one holds onto her; in a pressing situation, a loose hold with a wet hand is used.

paragraphs: Lo titbol beqoma zequpa, mippene sheyyesh meqomot asher mistatterim bah "y kak. veal tishcheh harbeh ad sheyyidbequ setareha zeh bazeh, ella shocheh meat, ad shettachat daddeha yihyeh nireh kederek shennireh beshaa shemmeniqa et benah; veenah tzerika leharchiq yarkoteha zo mizzo yoter midday, vegam lo leharchiq zerooteha mehaggup yoter midday, veyihyu kederek shehem beet hillukah.

clarification.explanation: She should not immerse standing fully upright, since this hides places the water cannot reach, but she also should not bend too much, so her folds of skin stick together. Rather she should bend slightly, in the manner she appears when nursing her child. She need not spread her thighs too far apart, nor hold her arms too far from her body, but rather keep them as they naturally are while walking.
takeaways: She immerses with a slight bend (neither fully upright nor overly bent).
Her limbs should be in a natural, walking-like position, neither pressed together nor too far apart.

paragraphs: Enah tzerika liptoach piha kede sheyyikkanesu hammayim, velo tiqpotz oto yoter midday, ella tashiq siptoteha zo lezo dibbuq benoni. v"g deim qaretza siptoteha lo aleta lah tebila kemo shekkatub bisip k"z, mikkol maqom im qaretza shinneha, la have chatzitza, kemo shekkatab "pitche teshuba", seip qatan y"g, beshem "chamude-daniyyel". velo taatzim eneha beyoter, deal yede kak naasim qematim lematta; vegam lo tiptach eneha beyoter, denaasim qematim lemala, ella tisgerem beripyon.

clarification.explanation: She need not open her mouth to let water in, nor clench it too tightly, but rather touch her lips together with moderate closure. If she pressed her lips tightly shut, her immersion is not valid, but clenching her teeth does not interpose. She should not close her eyes too tightly (creating folds below) nor open them too wide (creating folds above), but rather close them loosely.
takeaways: The mouth should be lightly closed, not clenched.
The eyes should be closed loosely, neither tightly shut nor too wide.

paragraphs: Lo titbol bayyom, vaapillu im tobelet bayyom hashshemini; veraq heka deikka ones gamur sheenah yekola litbol ballayla, titbol bayyom hashshemini; abal bayyom hashshebii lo titbol beshum open. vehakkelot, bitbila rishona shettobelin qodem hachuppa shei epshar litbol ballayla, tobelin bayyom hashshemini. ubishat haddechaq, kegon sheim yitacharu od, tihyeh habbia samuk levistah, o sheyyesh lahem hekreach acher, muttar shettitbol hakkalla tebila harishona sheqqodem hachuppa sheadayin lo haleka etzel baalah, bayyom hashshebii, deyesh lismok al hammattirim bezeh ki rabbim hemma, ukemo shekkatabti bsh"q "mqbtzl". umah shehittarnu litbol bayyom hashshebii, zeh eno ella lakkalla bitbila harishona davqa.

clarification.explanation: She should not immerse during the day — even when immersing on the eighth day — but only at night; and only when there is a genuine, unavoidable circumstance preventing night immersion should she immerse on the eighth day during the day, but on the seventh day she should never immerse under any circumstances. Brides at their first immersion before the wedding, for whom night immersion is impossible, immerse during the day on the eighth day. And in a pressing situation (if delaying would bring the union close to her veset, or another necessity) it is permitted for a bride to perform this first immersion on the seventh day, before going to her husband — but this applies specifically to a bride's first immersion.
takeaways: Immersion is at night; by unavoidable circumstance, on the eighth day, but never on the seventh.
A bride's first immersion may be on the eighth day, and in a pressing situation even the seventh.

paragraphs: Lo taamod al shum dabar hamqabbel tuma bishat tebila; laken im hammiqveh amoq harbeh, en mebiin keli vekopin oto al gabbayv kede shettaamod alayv, ella mesadderim abanim gedolot zo al gabbe zo veomedet alehen. ubemaqom shennahagu lishpok aleha mayim achar hattebila bitziatah min hammiqveh beod ragleha bemayim lechammem gupah, en limchot bahem; upoh irenu bagdad nohagim hetter bazeh. veyesh meqomot sheosin "mkynh" (mekona) etzel hammiqveh lechammem hammayim shebbo kede shettitbol bechammin mammash. vehinneh "g deyesh harbeh gedolim mattirim bekak, mikkol maqom maran za"l sheqqibbalnu horaotayv, pasaq kedaat hammachmirin, mishshum gezerat merchatzaot; veheerakti bazeh bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim"; amenam aach"k pasaqti lehattir dabar zeh beirenu "p dibre hari"p za"l besipro "nibchar mikkesep", siman y"z, shekkatab sham edut miggedole haddor, sheggam mera"n za"l asa maaseh lechammem hammiqveh, hepek mimmah shekkatab beshulchan aruk, siman' r", seip "h, yeuyyan sham. vekatab li yedidenu harab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu minni nr"v al minhag ir haqqodesh yerushalayim tvb"b, dehaashkenazzim hy"v, apillu bime haqqayitz mechammemim hammiqveh lehannashim, ki chosheshim pen mechamat haqqor enam tobelim karauy; vehasseparaddim hy"v, keshettobelin bemiqveh asher betok hammerchatz sheeno kol kak qar mechamat hebel hammerchatz, tobelin betzonen; aken lipamim shebbet-hammerchatz sagur o beyoqer, holekim litbol bemiqveh shel haashkenazzim shehu cham; ad kan debarayv nr"v.

clarification.explanation: She should not stand during immersion on something susceptible to ritual impurity; therefore in a deep mikveh one does not place a vessel to stand on, but arranges large stones instead. In places where it is customary to pour water on her to warm her body while she is in the mikveh — one should not protest, and this was also the Baghdad custom. In some places the mikveh water itself is heated by a machine; although some permit this, Maran ruled to be stringent due to the decree concerning bathhouses, but the rabbi ruled to permit it in his city based on testimony that Maran himself actually heated a mikveh. In Jerusalem, the Ashkenazim heat the mikveh even in summer, while the Sephardim immerse in cold water in a mikveh located within a hot bathhouse.
takeaways: One does not stand on a vessel susceptible to impurity — large stones are arranged instead.
The rabbi permitted heating the mikveh in his city, and customs vary on this.

paragraphs: "g dekatab mera"n za"l lebarek al hattebila qodem shettitbol - hamminhag pashut kemo shekkatab mvr"m za"l, shettitbol techilla tebila achat belo beraka, veaach"k beodah bemayim tebarek "asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu al hattebila", veachar habberaka titbol shenit. vetashgicha yapeh bitbila sheniyya zo shettihyeh kahogen, kaddat vekahalaka. upoh irenu bagdad y" nohagim hannashim litbol achar habberaka shalosh peamim, veyapeh osin, shebbazeh yotzeim yede chashashot hannizkarim beenayim ubappeh ubeshechayyat haggup vekayyotze - sheim lo naaset yapeh beachat, taaleh yapeh bashshenit o bashshelishit. vetob lehannicha sudar al roshah bishat habberaka, vetasir oto chabertah mealeha achar habberaka, vetitbol. vetob lomar pasuq "vayhi noam veku'" qodem habberaka.

clarification.explanation: The custom is that she first immerses once without a blessing, and then, while still in the water, recites the blessing "al hatevilah" and immerses a second time (taking care that the second immersion is done properly). In Baghdad it was customary to immerse three times after the blessing, and this is a good practice, since it removes all concerns (regarding the eyes, mouth, and posture) — if it was not done properly the first time, it will be valid on the second or third. It is good to place a scarf on her head during the blessing and remove it afterward, and to say "Vihi Noam" before the blessing.
takeaways: She immerses once, blesses in the water, and immerses again.
The Baghdad custom is to immerse three times after the blessing.

paragraphs: Tzarik shettihyeh haishsha tzenua lehastir tebilatah mibbene-adam; umi sheenah tzenua bekak, aleha neemar: "shokeb im behema". veim baalah bair, metzuvveh leishah shettitbol bizmannah; veen lebattel layla echad min periyya urebiyya; tze ulemad miyyehoshua, alayv hashshalom (megilla g.). vehamacheret tebilatah kede letzaer et balah, aneshah gadol meod; veayyen "chatam-soper", yoreh dea, siman q" vqtz"v. veim en balah bair vehiggia zeman tebilatah, lo titbol. veim yesh hekreach litbol mechamat ezeh sibba - katab "shebut-yaaqob" za"l, cheleq g', siman t"z, deminhagam shettannicha ballayla etzlah tinoq, vegam tannicha tachat hakkarim sakkin echad, yeuyyan sham. venistappaqti im minhagam zeh hu apillu im baalah bair, veraq oto layla yashan bebayit acher; veken im nitacher labo achar b' veg' lelot, im tzerika laasot ken bekol layla, o davqa belayla rishona; umin hassapeq - hachoshesh lazeh, yaaseh bekol gavna, vehabboteach baAdonai chesed yesobebennu.

Amar hamchabber: yesh letzarep im halakot ellu qetzat hilkot challa, hammuttelet gam ken al haishsha; ki keshem sheishsha tzerika lehizzaher harbeh behilkot nidda, kak tzerika lehizzaher behilkot challa.

clarification.explanation: A woman must be modest and conceal her immersion from other people. If her husband is in town, it is a mitzvah for her to immerse at her proper time, and she must not delay even a single night; one who delays her immersion to distress her husband incurs a great penalty. If her husband is not in town — she should not immerse. If there is a necessity to immerse when her husband is not in town, the custom is to place an infant with her at night and a knife under the pillows. (At the end, Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds that he will include here also a few laws of challah, since just as a woman is careful with the laws of niddah, so she should be careful with the laws of challah.)
takeaways: It is a mitzvah to immerse at the proper time, modestly and without delay.
If her husband is not in town, she should not immerse; if necessary, protective measures are taken.

paragraphs: Shiur issa shettitchayyeb bechalla hi sheba meot veshiba veshibim drh"m (yechidut mishqal - 3 garam veod), shekkak oleh cheshbon m"g betzim vechomesh betza, shehu shiur issa hachayyebet bachalla, ukemo shekkatab harab haggaon rabbenu chayyim palag'y za"l b"chayyim lerosh", dap q"y, ammud ', yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: The measure of dough obligated in challah is 777 dirhams of flour (a unit of weight of about three grams each), which comes to the equivalent of 43 and one-fifth eggs, the measure of dough obligated in challah.
takeaways: Dough is obligated in challah at a measure of 777 dirhams of flour (about 43 eggs).

paragraphs: Qodem shettaprish tebarek: asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu lehaprish challa teruma; veaach"k tomar "hare zo challa", vekaasher katabti bs"d behilkot shabbat haggadol, behilkot shana harishona.

clarification.explanation: Before separating challah, one blesses "who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to separate the challah tithe," and afterward says aloud "this is challah," in order to name it, as explained in the laws of the Great Sabbath.
takeaways: One blesses "to separate the challah tithe" and then says "this is challah."

paragraphs: Bazzeman hazzeh dechalla lisrepa azela, en lah shiur umaprishim dabar muat; beram rabbenu haari"y zlh"h sebira leh, gam bazzeman hazzeh yedaqdequ lehaprish echad min arbaim ushemona, vekannizkar beshaar-taame-hammitzot, shalach-leka, yeuyyan sham. vekatab rabbenu chida" za"l b"birke yosep", shello raa velo shama shum chasid noheg bazeh, ayyen sham. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti: kevan derabbenu haggadol amar ken, tob sheyyaaseh haadam paam achat bashshana ki dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, veyaaseh zot haish beatzmo, leqayyem paam achat haprashat chala beyado. vedabar beitto mah tob, lehosip zekut al zekiyyotayv qodem yom hakkippurim.

clarification.explanation: In our time, since the challah portion is burned (due to impurity) and not eaten, it has no fixed measure, and only a small amount is separated. But the Arizal held that even in our time one should be meticulous to separate one forty-eighth. The Chida wrote he did not see the pious following this practice, but the rabbi wrote that since the Arizal said so, it is good for a person to do this himself once a year, to add merit before Yom Kippur.
takeaways: In our time, only a small amount of challah is separated, with no fixed measure.
It is good to be meticulous once a year and separate one forty-eighth, following the Arizal, for merit before Yom Kippur.

paragraphs: Haoseh issa kede lebashshelah o letaggenah, maprishin mimmenna challa belo beraka; veim rotzin leepot qetzat mimmenna, maprishin bibraka. vehallash issa bechalab bilbad belo mayim, yesh pelugta, laken yaprish belo beraka; veayyen "lebush", hilkot pesach, siman ts"b, seip v'.

clarification.explanation: One who makes dough in order to cook or fry it separates challah from it without a blessing; but if one wishes to bake part of it — one separates with a blessing. And one who kneads dough with milk alone, without water — there is a dispute whether it is obligated in challah, and therefore one should separate without a blessing.
takeaways: Dough for cooking/frying — challah without a blessing; for baking — with a blessing.
Dough made with milk alone — separated without a blessing, due to the doubt.

paragraphs: Im bechu"l shakach lehaprish challa beereb-shabbat, okelin beshabbat, umeshayyerin kikkar o chetzyo, kede lehaprish mimmennu challa bachol veyishshaer mimmennu, debaenan sheyyehe sheyareha nikkarin. ubeeretz-yisrael sheshshakechu lehaprish veakelu rob happat bibli daat, yaprish mehammuttar al hakkol, gam al mah sheakal, letaqqen mah deepshar, dibdiabad maprish shello min hammuqqap, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu chida" "bebirke yosep", siman shk"g, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: Outside the Land of Israel, if one forgot to separate challah on the Sabbath eve — one eats on the Sabbath and leaves over a loaf or half of it in order to separate challah from it on a weekday, since a noticeable remainder must be left. And in the Land of Israel, where they forgot to separate and unknowingly ate most of the bread — one separates from the remainder on behalf of the whole, including what was already eaten, to rectify what is possible, since after the fact one may separate even not from adjoining dough.
takeaways: Outside Israel: one eats and leaves a loaf for separation on a weekday.
In Israel: one separates from the remainder on behalf of the whole, even what was already eaten.

paragraphs: Yesh nashim sheddarkan lalush shette issot: achat, belilatah aba sheopin otah mine mezonot; veachat, belilatah rakka sheopin otah kikkerot lechem; vetabo baalat-habbayit vetaprish challa meachat mehem utebarek, veachar shaa tabo vetaprish min hashshenit utebarek - hare zeh asur, dehu beraka sheenah tzerika, shetztzerika lehaprish mishshenehem yachad bibraka; veayyen "tebuat-shor", siman y"t, seip qatan t"z, v"lebushe-serad", bechiddushe dinim leyoreh dea, ot qy"t. ak im baalat-habbayit mazmenet ishah acheret lehaprish min hachalla hashshenit ulebarek, yesh letzadded depanim chadashot bau lekan. umiddibre harab "mechoqeq-yeuddeh", hilkot pesach, siman tl"b, b"chuqqe-daat", seip qatan g', mashma daarik lemebad haki, yeuyyan sham. ak nireh li deen lismok al zeh, veyesh lachush gam bikhay gavna libraka sheenah tzerika - kevan deissa hashshenit hayeta lipne baalat-habbayit beet shebberaka al haachat; vaapillu im taaseh beopen zeh, ditchilla taaseh et chabertah shalicha lehaprish min harakka bilbad, veaach"k hi tabo vetaprish min heabeh, gam ken yesh lachush, laken gam bikhay gavna habberaka hi achat.

clarification.explanation: A woman who kneaded two batches of dough (one thick for pastries and one soft for bread), and separated challah from one with a blessing, and an hour later from the other with a blessing — this is a blessing said unnecessarily, since she should have separated from both together with a single blessing. Even if she summons another woman to separate and bless over the second batch — one should not rely on this leniency, since the second batch was already before her at the time of the first blessing, and therefore the blessing over both batches is a single one.
takeaways: Challah is separated from both batches of dough together, with a single blessing.
One may not split the blessing between two batches that were both already present, even through another woman.
